evidence: Old wording "(as described in Noticing Counts)" claims the reader has already seen that section; in the guide Noticing Counts (line 205) comes after If You Want to Kill Yourself (line 131), so a reader would look back for something not yet read. New wording "(more on that in Noticing Counts, further on)": "that" has a clear antecedent (noticing who's doing the noticing, in the same sentence), "further on" fixes the direction, and the parenthetical keeps the pointer, the instruction and the borrowed adult. "Further on" is Joel's own phrase elsewhere in the guide (lines 623, 629). It reads as casual and as the same author, adds no claim or promise beyond that more exists. Slight redundancy of "more" plus "further on" is natural speech, not a tell. No inventory row applies: not T19 (it is a pointer to a real section, not an announcement), T11, T22, T15 or C02.
